newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firm on bank borrowing.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firm on bank borrowing.

text.p: Interbank rates were firmer on Monday due to borrowings by small banks and finance companies, dealers said.
"Though liquidity has improved, the small banks and finance houses were again pushing up rates," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Dealers said payments for weekly government treasury bills also firmed rates.
The one-, two- and three-week money were at 7.70/80 percent against 7.50/70 on Friday, dealers said.
The one-month rate was at 7.60/90 percent from 7.50/60, while three- and six-month money were at 7.50/80 percent against 7.50/60.
A shortage of funds at the short-end of the market would keep the overnight interbank rate firm, dealers said.
The overnight closed at 7.50/8.0 percent on Friday.
Dealers said Bank Negara was believed to have injected funds, through an agent bank, last week to improve market liquidity. No confirmation was available.
Bank Negara's massive intervention to defend the ringgit last month had led to a liquidity squeeze, pushing interbank rates to unusually high levels.
There will be a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Tuesday but this will be matched by a maturity of an issue of a similar amount on Friday, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board, futures dealers said.
At 0300 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down five points to 92.43, or an implied yield of 7.57 percent.
September contract fell four to 92.55, or 7.45 percent while December was down two to 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
